rv: Awesome film about what the dumbfounded army nurse guy should do when confronted by a woman about to give birth at home when all he was assigned to do is take the dame to the hospital. A very messy birth comes forth. Lots of blood. That's gonna be some cleanup.The narrato also advises the chap to say to the mother she's got a lovely boy. What if it isn't? WHAT IF IT ISN'T??? Better then that similar titled childbirth movie on here. This is a MUST SEE on this site!

Its totally real - my health teacher, Mr VanCamp showed this film for years, apparently after he’d been told to scrap it for something less graphic. I saw it in ‘88, sent to the principal for passing out / who sent me to the nurse and asked me if ‘VanCamp was showing that awful birth flick to 9th graders again’. Yes he is, my man. Poor VC on ‘sabbatical’ for the next 3 years at least. I still blame myself for diming the old guy out. Tyranny. Beauty flick, 5 stars.

gov.archives.arc.47087: This film documents daily life in the small, rural community of Holtville, Alabama.

rv: I grew up here and so did my Father. The movie tells the story of a project where the school was used to transform the community. While the casual viewer might have a different opinion of the movie, it is wonderful for those of us who grew up and went to the school or who lived in the agrarian South. The movie portrays one facet of rural life in the South. I am happy to see my Grandfather, parents and family friends come to life! I was not born when the movie was made but saw it many times as a student at Holtville. My parents both taught school there.
